subject.title: [Feature]: Mobile apps: per-gateway custom headers for gateways behind authenticating proxies

question: Should OpenClaw accept per-gateway credential HTTP headers in the Android mobile app under the same security boundaries already merged for iOS?
rationale: The remaining work changes credential storage and gateway transport headers, and the issue already carries maintainer, security, and auth-provider labels, so automation should not decide the product/security boundary.

options.title: Approve Android parity after security review
options.body: Land the linked Android PR if secure storage, TLS-only injection, sanitizer, reset cleanup, and non-gateway isolation proof satisfy owner/security review, then close this issue.

options.title: Narrow the supported mobile scope
options.body: Keep iOS support and ask for a smaller Android design or documented limitation if Android secure storage or transport constraints are not acceptable yet.

options.title: Reject mobile custom headers
options.body: Close the platform PRs and document that authenticating reverse proxies must be handled outside mobile apps, accepting the blocked deployment shape.

recommendation.title: Approve Android parity after security review
recommendation.body: Land the linked Android PR if secure storage, TLS-only injection, sanitizer, reset cleanup, and non-gateway isolation proof satisfy owner/security review, then close this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the issue plus both platform implementation threads and can route the owner/security review context to the right platform reviewers.
